People: Aeschylus (author, Wikidata Q40939), died -456; Sophocles (author, Wikidata Q7235), died -406; Goldwin Smith (translator, Wikidata Q3110133), died 1910. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Aeschylus, 526 BCE-457 BCE; Sophocles, 496? BCE-407 BCE; Smith, Goldwin, 1823-1910 [Translator]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: Specimens of Greek Tragedy, Macmillan and Co., 1893, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/specimensgreekt00sophgoog. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 78%, 80%, 82% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Aeschylus, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
